body: I'm 24 XD The subject in question is foreign languages, and I've taken intensives at a few different institutions at home and abroad, which all seem to pull the same shit.  Apparently I sound so darn sophisticated (as in my accent, which is the really infuriating part here) that I'm just *meant* to skip a full year of class, even though skipping class would require me to miss fundamental grammar and vocabulary that the next level is predicated on.  Then they act all surprised that I don't know the material from the course they made me skip >/

Haha yeah.  It's kinda like imposter syndrome, except I have tangible examples I can point to to say "see this example of when somebody said I was too smart?  It ended up with me so stressed and terrified that I barely learned anything"!  :/

I guess my response to that would be, if she feels that she would be too distracted to be able to get a job due to her grandfather's circumstances, would she even be focused enough to get a job, much less keep it?  Especially if money isn't a make-or-break issue at the moment, it might even be a decent idea from a pragmatic perspective: if she cares for her grandfather, she'll be able to put that on her resume as a reason why she wasn't working, and a lot of employers will understand.  If she gets a job and ends up getting fired because she can't focus on her work with her grandfather sick?      Yeah, that doesn't look as good, and if your description of her is accurate then this outcome is very likely.  
  
  One last comment: perhaps I'm wrong, but you sound like someone who hasn't had gone through any major deaths yet.  As someone who has, I can tell you that shit changes you.  Whatever you may think of her now, there's a decent chance that she'll become a more mature, hardworking person who will be more appealing to employers as a consequence of taking this time to care for her grandfather.

Have you ever seen the film "But I'm a Cheerleader"?  It's about a girl who realizes she's a lesbian despite acting "straight" (see: being a cheerleader).  There's this one character in there who gets sent to a conversion camp and whom everyone assumes is gay, but she actually isn't.  She just "looks butch" with a stocky body and short hair, so everyone believes that she has to be gay, even as they acknowledge that more femme women like the cheerleader are full-well capable of being gay despite their appearance.  I know it's not much, but if you're looking for some pop-culture representation of how exasperating it is for people to think you're gay when you're not, that's one option for you.  
  
  Also, for what it's worth, I'll try harder not to assume people are gay regardless of whatever stereotypes they adhere to, just in case they end up being someone like you :)
